Every figure `wdm plots` draws for the current diet, from the real record as of {{< meta bw.as_of >}}, regenerated with the [presentation](weight-dynamics.html)'s numbers whenever new days are logged; nothing here is drawn by hand. Each caption says how to read its figure. Click or tap a figure to open it full screen and zoom in.

## Weight and body composition

![**Weight trajectory.** Raw weigh-ins (gray), the smoothed trend, and its 95% band. The trend is what moved; the scatter of a pound or more around it is mostly water and gut contents. Judge progress by the trend's slope over a week or more, never by one morning.](assets/wdm/trajectory.svg)

![**Body composition.** Estimated fat and lean mass with their 95% bands. Fat mass enters the dynamics only through the energy density of the tissue lost, so a scale identifies it weakly: read the bands, and the trend rather than the level. Weekly waist readings narrow the fat band somewhat.](assets/wdm/composition.svg)

## The plan

![**Today's plan.** Top: prescribed intake by week, stacked as protein, carbohydrate and fat. Bottom: predicted scale weight and tissue mass, continuing the filtered trend up to today (faded). The gap between the two lines is water. Only the first day is a prescription; tomorrow the plan is remade and the rest changes.](assets/wdm/plan.svg)

![**Adherence.** Top: energy and each macronutrient eaten on each finished day (dots) against the prescription from the plans log (line), with the range within 10% of it shaded; titles count the days inside that range, and the latest values are labeled. Energy is on the label scale `wdm log` shows, before the model's fiber correction. Bottom: the running total of energy eaten above or below plan. That is the panel to watch: a line climbing steadily means the weight will come off more slowly than planned. A macronutrient off on a day when energy is on plan matters less: low protein risks lean mass over weeks, and carbohydrate moves water from day to day, but neither changes how much is lost.](assets/wdm/adherence.svg)

## What the model has learned

![**Parameter evolution.** What the filter believed about each of the nine metabolic parameters, day by day, relative to its prior center (dashed line at 1), with a 90% band. Each day uses only the record up to that morning. Read the band's width: a band as wide as it started has learned nothing, whatever its median does. A band that has narrowed and moved off the line is where the data have spoken.](assets/wdm/parameter_evolution.svg)

![**Maintenance.** Energy spent at each day's trend weight, $c_0 + c_1 W$, as the filter estimated it (90% band), against the logged intake on the same axis; the vertical gap between them is the day's deficit. The band is narrow even when the two coefficients behind it are not, because their errors are strongly correlated ([why](docs/theory/estimation.md#identifiability)).](assets/wdm/maintenance.svg)

## Diagnostics and inputs

![**Innovations.** Each weigh-in's one-step-ahead surprise, in standard deviations, over time and as a histogram. An adequate model's are centered on zero with a standard deviation near 1 and no pattern. A histogram wider than the reference curve means the noise is understated and the intervals overconfident; a weekly pattern usually means weekend eating the log misses ([Troubleshooting](docs/reading-output.md#troubleshooting)).](assets/wdm/innovations.svg)

![**Intake log.** The inputs no other figure shows, as logged: exercise energy, fiber, sodium, and steps. Unlogged days are gaps, not the habitual values the model substitutes. Steps are a diagnostic only; they do not enter the energy balance.](assets/wdm/intake_log.svg)
